harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every sudo command (user, timestamp, command) to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log via /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-logfile (Defaults logfile, log_input, log_output, !syslog), keeping command details out of /var/log/secure. Added logrotate for the new file. Verified pre- and post-reboot that the config, log file, and correct routing all survive a full node restart.
actions_performed: Created /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-logfile with logfile, log_input/log_output, and !syslog directives; validated with visudo -cf
Ran test sudo commands and confirmed entries appear in the dedicated log with user/timestamp/command, and do not appear as command-level entries in /var/log/secure or /var/log/messages
Captured pre-restart boot_id and config/log health baseline
Restarted node1 via sudo systemctl reboot (non-blocking ack)
Polled node1 until reachable; confirmed boot_id changed (95e2f83d... -> 414ae4e3...)
Post-restart: reconfirmed sudoers drop-in intact/valid, log file persisted with prior entries, new sudo command correctly appended to dedicated log, and secure log still shows no COMMAND= entries

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands logged with user and timestamp to dedicated file /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Config created and validated (visudo -cf parsed OK); test sudo commands produced timestamped entries with USER=root, invoking user antrieb, and COMMAND= in the dedicated log

evidence.requirement: Entries kept out of general system log (/var/log/secure, /var/log/messages)
evidence.summary: Before and after reboot, tail of /var/log/secure showed only generic PAM session opened/closed lines with no COMMAND= text; explicit grep for COMMAND= in secure log post-reboot returned no matches

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline capture (boot identity + service/config health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 95e2f83d-06d0-47d9-8151-0f56c34060f1, confirmed sudoers drop-in parses OK and log file exists with correct perms and 28 existing lines
systemctl reboot launched via backgrounded/disowned nohup; command returned 'reboot acknowledged and triggered' before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart / proof restart occurred
evidence.summary: Immediate follow-up poll timed out connecting to node1, confirming the node was down mid-restart

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves actual restart (not just service restart)
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as 414ae4e3-13e0-41ed-8a72-2a32990d5249, differing from the pre-restart 95e2f83d-... value

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo logging config, log data, and correct routing
evidence.summary: Sudoers drop-in still present and valid; log file persisted with prior 28+ lines (now 36); new sudo id command correctly appended with timestamp/user/command; secure log still free of COMMAND= entries
